General information.Name: Environmental Impacts Associated with the Production and Packing of Persian Lemon in Mexico through Life-Cycle Assessment
General information.Category: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting/111 Crop Production/111320 Citrus (except Orange) Groves
General information.Description: In this study, the environmental impacts associated with the intensive production of Persian lemons are assessed, including the agricultural and packing phases of the fresh fruit. A life-cycle assessment (LCA) tool was used in accordance with the ISO 14040 and 14044 standards and implemented in SimaPro PhD (9.2) software. The life-cycle inventory database was primarily composed of data collected during field visits to local lemon orchards and the main packing company in the region. The functional unit was defined as 1 kg of packed fresh Persian lemons. The selected impact categories were the carbon footprint, water footprint, and energy footprint, and the results obtained for the defined functional unit were 405.8 g CO2 eq, 40.3 L of water, and 5.9 MJ, respectively. The industrial packing phase of the fruits had a greater impact on the carbon and energy footprints, mostly due to the manufacturing of packaging materials and cardboard boxes, followed by the transportation of supplies. Regarding the water footprint, the agricultural phase was identified as the most significant contributor to water consumption, primarily attributed to maintenance operations and the application of agrochemicals.
General information.Tags: lemon production, life-cycle assessment, carbon, water and energy footprint, environmental impacts
General information.Technology Description: The life-cycle assessment (LCA) was implemented in SimaPro PhD (9.2) software. The life-cycle inventory was built using primary data from field visits and secondary data from literature and the Ecoinvent 3.8 database. The impact assessment methods used were: IPCC GWP 100a for the carbon footprint (based on ISO14067), the ReCiPe methodology (v. 1.01) for the water footprint (based on ISO 14046), and the cumulative energy demand (CED) method for the energy footprint.

processDocumentation.LCI method: The methodology was based on the guidelines of the ISO 14040:2006 and ISO 14044:2006 standards, including the phases: definition of goal and scope, life-cycle inventory analysis (LCI), life-cycle impact assessment (LCIA), and interpretation of results.
processDocumentation.Modeling constants: The scope of the LCA was 'from cradle to gate'. The product system considered the cultivation, harvesting, and packaging of the Persian lemon ready for distribution. The supply of required inputs and their transport were included, as well as the supplied energy. Capital goods such as facilities and infrastructure were not included, while agricultural implements were considered. Load allocations by mass were applied for the distribution of environmental impacts.
processDocumentation.Data source information: Primary data was collected through fieldwork (interviews with farmers, traders, entrepreneurs, and specialists) and field visits to a nursery, two large producers, and a packing facility. Secondary data were supplemented with information from specialized literature and the Ecoinvent 3.8 database, which was adapted and updated with locally collected data.
processDocumentation.Data completeness: The product system comprised two phases: (i) the agricultural stage, with three sub-stages—seedbed, nursery, and orchard; and (ii) the citrus industrial stage, with two sub-stages—processing and packing. Capital goods such as facilities and infrastructure were excluded.
processDocumentation.Data selection: The study focused on intensive production of Persian lemons in a specific region in Mexico. Data were collected from representative producers and the main packing company in the region.
processDocumentation.Data treatment: The collected data were processed with material and energy balances to verify the data's suitability, and then quantified with respect to the functional unit. Load allocations by mass were applied for the distribution of environmental impacts generated in the products and co-products.
processDocumentation.Sampling procedure: Approximately 30 field visits were conducted over a three-month period. The process comprised: (i) reconnaissance of the study area to identify intensive producers; (ii) construction and distribution of questionnaires to farmers to acquire firsthand cultivation techniques; and (iii) replication of this procedure at the main packing company.
processDocumentation.Data collection period: Data collection was conducted over a three-month period. The article was published in May 2024.
processDocumentation.Use advice: The results are specific to the intensive production practices of Persian lemon in the studied region of Mexico. The study excludes capital goods like facilities and infrastructure, which should be considered when applying the results.
processDocumentation.Completeness: High for the defined cradle-to-gate scope, with the explicit exclusion of capital goods like facilities and infrastructure.

processDocumentation.Intended application: To generate valuable knowledge for decision makers in regions engaged in the intensive production of Persian lemon, contributing to the mitigation of associated environmental impacts. Furthermore, it aims to disseminate relevant information among scientists with expertise and interest in the field, commercial importers, and an informed public, thereby encouraging socially responsible consumption practices.
